content.text:
Prompts are now escaped before they go into the Piton anchor, and names you reference are auto-imported even when the prompt was pasted in. All tests pass (166, 1 ignored). I haven't tried typing or pasting into the running app.

**The problem:** the prompt was written into the anchor as raw Piton prose. I tested the installed `piton` with pasted-style text:
- **Read as structure:** `key:`, `- item`, `"…"`, `1 + 2` and `true` at the start of a line were read as Piton structure, not text.
- **Breaks the compile:** any `{…}` or `${…}` was evaluated, and an unmatched `{` or `"` or a line starting a ``` fence is a syntax error. Extra indentation is an error too.
- **Silently changed:** `// …` was cut off as a comment.
- **Backslashes:** every backslash is dropped, so `C:\Users` becomes `C:Users`. Piton's own spec says `\\` should give one backslash, so this looks like a bug in the `piton` compiler. I didn't change Piton; you may want to look at it there.

**How prompts are written now:** each line of the prompt is a list of pieces.
- **Text:** the text between references is a quoted string, with quotes, backslashes and `${` escaped, so it compiles exactly as written.
- **References:** `@{Name…}` and `${Name.path}` stay real references only when `Name` is imported. Anything else, like a pasted `${HOME}` or a typo'd `@{NotImported}`, is plain text. A mistyped reference therefore goes through as text; before, it was a compile error.
- **What the harness gets:** exactly what you typed or pasted, including line breaks and indentation, with references turned into links. Before, single line breaks were joined into spaces.
- **System prompts** from the templates are written the same way.
- **Old saved prompts** in your history and queue, which are still in the old format, read back fine.

**Auto-imports:**
- **What was failing:** these pastes stopped `piton lsp` from auto-importing a reference: an unmatched quote, a ``` line, deeper indentation, or text after `//`.
- **The fix:** the language server now sees a separate copy of the prompt. References and words are kept, and everything else is blanked out character for character. Cursor positions still line up, so completion keeps working.

**Tests added:**
- **The big one:** a prompt full of Piton-looking text, backslashes, tabs, a fence, an imported reference and an unimported one. It checks the prompt saves, reads back and compiles to exactly the input, with only the real reference resolved.
- **Auto-import:** a test runs six pasted cases through the real language server. Four of them fail without the blanking, and all six pass with it.
- **Unit tests:** how a line splits into text and references, and that blanking keeps every position.
- **Existing tests:** completion, auto-import, queue, history and attached text all still pass.

**Spec:** `spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi` has new `escaping` and `autoImports` sections under the hidden anchor. `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, and the app builds with no warnings. The code changes are in `src/hidden_anchor.rs` and `src/piton_lsp.rs`.
